title: Basic Prepositions for Place and Time
goal: Choose basic Norwegian prepositions for simple places, movement, visits, future time, past time, and duration.

objectives.statement: Choose basic Norwegian prepositions for simple places, movement, visits, future time, past time, and duration.

spans.value: Maja and Jonas are arranging to meet after work. Their friend Nora may join them later.
Jeg er på jobb. Jeg drar om ti minutter.

blocks.translation: I’m at work. I’m leaving in ten minutes.

spans.value: Kan du møte meg på kafeen ved stasjonen?

blocks.translation: Can you meet me at the café by the station?
Yes, I’m walking to the café.

spans.value: Nora er hos legen nå. Hun kommer om en time.

blocks.translation: Nora is at the doctor’s now. She is coming in an hour.

spans.value: Var hun ikke hos legen for to dager siden?

blocks.translation: Wasn’t she at the doctor’s two days ago?

spans.value: Jo. Hun var syk i tre dager, så hun har en ny time.

blocks.translation: Yes, she was. She was ill for three days, so she has another appointment.

spans.value: Greit. Jeg jobbet på kontoret i ni timer i dag. Jeg blir på kafeen i en time.

blocks.translation: All right. I worked at the office for nine hours today. I’ll stay at the café for an hour.

Choosing the right preposition or time frame lets you distinguish being somewhere from going somewhere, future time from past time, and duration from other time relationships. ## Being in a place: i and på {#being-in-a-place role=model objectives=obj-basic-prepositions-place-time-01}

with many enclosed places and with towns, cities, and countries:

en.value: I am in the shop.
She lives in Oslo.

The children are playing in the park.

spans.value: in many familiar expressions connected with workplaces, schools, offices, cafés, and activities:

en.value: Jonas is at work.
Maja is at the café.
The teacher is at the school.
We are at the office.

spans.value: These are useful phrase patterns, not a perfect geometric system. A person can physically be inside both a shop and a café, but ordinary Norwegian commonly says

en.value: She works in Oslo.
She works at the office.
We are meeting in the park.
We are meeting at the café.

because someone is physically inside it. Norwegian often chooses the preposition according to the conventional expression and the activity associated with the place.
The next decision is whether someone is already in a place or moving toward it.

en.value: I am walking to the café.
She is travelling to Oslo.
We are driving to the shop.

spans.value: Compare the destination with the resulting location:

Maja is travelling to Oslo.

spans.value: In each sentence, the time expression gives the duration of the activity. ## Back at the café {#back-at-the-cafe role=model objectives=obj-basic-prepositions-place-time-01}
Jonas has now arrived. Maja sends Nora a message.
Jonas er på kafeen nå. Hvor er du?

blocks.translation: Jonas is at the café now. Where are you?

spans.value: Nei, det går fint. Jeg går til kafeen.

blocks.translation: No, that’s fine. I’m walking to the café.

spans.value: Bra. Vi blir her i en time.

blocks.translation: Good. We are staying here for an hour.

prompt.value: To Nora: Write a message in Norwegian. Lars is at the library now. Sara is going to the doctor's office. Omar is spending the afternoon with his grandmother. It is Sunday, and the meeting starts in three hours. Eva came home two days ago. The course lasts two hours. Put the information naturally.

payload.judge_prompt: Assess the message purpose, all six facts and natural Norwegian prepositional expressions for location, destination, visiting a person, future and past time, and duration. Accept both «på biblioteket» and «i biblioteket» for Lars, and both «hos bestemoren» and «besøker bestemoren» for Omar.

criteria.instruction: Svaret er en sammenhengende norsk melding til Nora som forklarer hvor folk er og når hendelser skjer.
Meldingen formidler alle de seks opplysningene fra oppgaven med riktig betydning.
Uses natural Norwegian expressions for location, destination, visiting a person, future time, past time, and duration. Accept «hos bestemoren» or «besøker bestemoren» for Omar.

text.value: «Kan du fortelle meg hvor folk er, og hva som skjer senere?»
«Ja, jeg sender deg en samlet oppdatering.»

prompt.value: It is Sunday at 4 p.m. Aino is at the station, Mikkel is going to the dentist, and Liv is spending the afternoon with her uncle. The train leaves at 4:20. Anders came home after school on Friday, and the concert lasts 90 minutes. Write Nora a message with this information.

payload.judge_prompt: Check that the message conveys all six updates accurately, using natural expressions for location, destination, visiting a person, a future time, a past time, and duration. Accept departure at 16.20 or «om 20 minutter».

criteria.instruction: Meldingen formidler alle de seks opplysningene med riktig betydning.

prompt.value: You are Mina. Write in the first person. It is Saturday at 10 a.m. Send a friend a message in Norwegian about the trip. You are at the library now, leave for Trondheim in 20 minutes, and will stay there for three days with your brother. Your brother visited Bergen one month earlier. Use natural expressions for location, departure, destination, duration, and an earlier time.

payload.judge_prompt: Vurder om meldingen formidler Minas nåværende sted, avreise klokka 10.20 (eller om 20 minutter), reisemål, tre dagers opphold hos broren og brorens besøk i Bergen én måned tidligere.

criteria.instruction: Meldingen formidler alle opplysningene med riktig betydning.
Meldingen bruker naturlige norske uttrykk for nåværende sted, framtidig tidspunkt, reisemål, varighet og et tidligere tidspunkt.

text.value: «Kan du fortelle meg om lørdagsturen din?»
«Ja, jeg sender deg en kort melding.»
